title: APTEL Restores Rs. 5.68/kWh Tariff, Holds Haryana Commission Could Not Reopen a Settled Rate
case_name: Appeal concerning the Haryana Power Purchase Centre's challenge to the tariff payable to Siwana Solar Power Projects Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: The Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission had raised the tariff payable to a 5 MW solar project in Bhiwani from Rs. 5.68 to Rs. 6.44 per kWh, years after the rate was first settled. APTEL set aside that revision, holding the tariff question had already been decided between the same parties and could not be reopened. It restored the original Rs. 5.68 per kWh rate as binding.
card_tip: Once a tariff dispute between a discom-side body and a generator has been finally decided, do not expect a state commission's later order to reopen it; raise res judicata early rather than relitigating the rate.
verification_notes: The 18 September 2026 decision date, the bench of Seema Gupta and Virender Bhat, the 5 MW Siwana project in Bhiwani, Haryana, the original Rs. 5.68/kWh rate, and the setting aside of HERC's Rs. 6.44/kWh revision are consistent across Mercom India's and SolarQuarter's reports. Neither source gives a confirmed case caption or appeal number, so the case_name here is a descriptive label rather than a verified citation; the order itself was not independently retrieved.
